 Giannis Antetokounmpo finished Sunday’s win over the Kings with 29 points (14-of-23 FGs, 1-of-7 FTs), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks.
 While Giannis had a brutal night at the foul line, fantasy managers rostering the Heat forward know they’ll likely have to punt on free-throw percentage. Against the Kings, he made up for the poor night at the foul line with excellent shooting from the field and big numbers in rebounds, steals and blocks. The Heat play three games in Week 4, starting with the Jazz on Tuesday in the final game of Miami’s road trip.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, two steals and three blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers. 
 On most nights, fantasy managers can expect Giannis to shoot a high percentage from the field but struggle at the foul line. The opposite happened against the Clippers, with the Heat forward shooting 40 percent from the field and 84.6 percent from the foul line. Antetokounmpo finished with a robust stat line that had everything but a three-pointer. The Heat play two more games this week, starting with the Warriors on Thursday.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 30 points (10-of-17 FGs, 10-of-15 FTs), 12 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, two blocks and seven turnovers in a 138-117 loss to the Lakers on Monday. 
 Giannis wasn’t able to match his production from Friday’s big win, but he was still able to score at least 30 points for the fourth time in seven games this year. Of course, free throws continue to be an issue, but Giannis is too good in other categories for it to matter much. Miami’s two-game winning streak is over, and they’ll need Giannis to continue to dominate to get back on track as their five-game west coast road trip continues on Wednesday.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo finished Friday’s win over the Pacers with 31 points (13-of-18 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 17 rebounds, 10 assists, one block and one three-pointer. 
 The Pacers had no answer for Giannis on Friday, as he scored 24 of his 31 points in the paint. The partnership between Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo looked a bit awkward at the start of the season, which isn’t surprising. But both have looked more comfortable in the last two games, both Heat victories. And it helps that the Heat shot 18-of-40 from three against the Pacers, which provided much-needed spacing on offense.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points (11-of-18 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), 18 rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in Wednesday’s 129-117 victory over the Hawks. 
 Antetokounmpo’s fantasy production hadn’t suffered despite the slow start by his new team the Heat. After an 0-4 start to the season, Miami finally picked up its first win against the Hawks Wednesday. Antetokounmpo was excellent again as he grabbed a game-high 18 rebounds, which was at least twice as many as anyone else.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 29 points (12-of-23 FGs, 3-of-7 FTs), 15 rebounds, 11 assists, one block, two three-pointers and five turnovers in a 113-109 loss to the Mavericks on Monday. 
 Giannis dominated this game early on and nearly had a triple-double before halftime, and he was able to secure his first one with the Heat just a few minutes into the third quarter. However, it wasn’t enough to get their first win of the season. Giannis was much better than he was in Saturday’s loss to Charlotte, but he didn’t get much help from his co-star Bam Adebayo, who was held to just eight points. Antetokounmpo should continue to post gaudy stat lines, and they’ll head to Atlanta for their next game on Wednesday.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists and one steal against the Hornets on Saturday. 
 So far this season, the story for Miami has been that Giannis hasn’t had enough help. Well, his teammates stepped up more in this game, but Antetokounmpo wasn’t quite as productive. They went on a big run without him to tie things up in the fourth quarter. He entered with about four minutes left, committed two fouls in three minutes, and the Hornets took a six-point lead. It was a rough performance for him, but there is no reason for managers to worry. He averaged 35.5 points through their first two games and should get back on track against the Mavericks on Monday.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo had 36 points (15-of-26 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Pistons. 
 Antetokounmpo has now had at least 35 points in each of his first two games in a Heat uniform. He played a more complete game across the stat sheet compare to the opener with 12 rebounds, five assists and three stocks. Still, the Heat lost to the Pistons by 17 after dropping the opener to the Timberwolves by 25. Miami will look for its first win of the season and probably get it against the reeling Hornets in Charlotte on Saturday.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 35 points (13-of-19 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 Giannis came out hot in his official Heat debut, scoring 14 points in the first quarter. He went into the halftime break with 21, but no other Heat player scored more than seven. Antetokounmpo finished with a solid stat line, but fantasy managers may have hoped for more on the defensive end. The Heat host the Pistons Friday in the first of two games in as many nights before visiting Charlotte on Saturday.

 Keegan Murray (ankle) accounted for 10 points (3-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), one rebound, two assists, two steals and one block in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
 Making his first appearance since October 23, Murray played a reserve role on Sunday. After playing stints of six, four and five minutes in the first three quarters, the Kings forward played the last 7:46 of the fourth quarter. Murray took a hard fall during the second quarter when he landed on his upper back after a Bobby Portis shot fake got him in the air, but he did not require any attention on the Kings’ bench. As Murray’s minutes increase, Precious Achiuwa (7/14/2/1 with one block) will likely see his minutes decrease after logging 36 minutes on Sunday.

 Zach LaVine recorded 15 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
 LaVine shot the ball well on Sunday, but the playing time was an eye-opener. He played 25 minutes against the Heat and did not return after being subbed out with 4:03 remaining in the third quarter. The Kings made no injury announcement, and LaVine was called for one foul, so foul trouble couldn’t have been the reason. Kings head coach Doug Christie played Darius Acuff Jr. and Malik Monk (9/2/3/1) in the backcourt for the entire fourth quarter, which left no room for LaVine. That’s something for fantasy managers to watch moving forward.

 Darius Acuff Jr. tallied 32 points (11-of-21 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
 Against one of the NBA’s better perimeter defenders, Miami’s Davion Mitchell, Acuff posted one of the best stat lines of his rookie season on Sunday. Shooting over 50 percent from the field, the Kings guard recorded his second 30-point double-double. While Acuff recorded five turnovers, he did a good job navigating the two-man game throughout Sunday’s defeat. The Kings play three games next week, starting with the Magic on Tuesday.

 Davion Mitchell accounted for 17 points (6-of-11 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, 11 assists, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 Playing against the franchise that selected him in the first round of the 2021 draft, Mitchell had one of his best games of the season on Sunday. In addition to recording his sixth double-double of the season, “Off Night” matched his season high with 11 assists. Rostered in 82 percent of Yahoo leagues, Mitchell’s fantasy value exceeds his ADP by a significant margin, and that may not change anytime soon.

 Bam Adebayo produced 18 points (7-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 After a slow start to the season, Adebayo has scored at least 18 points in three straight and six of Miami’s last seven games. Against the Kings, he did most of his damage in the first half, recording a 16/5/2/2 line while shooting 6-of-9 from the field. In the second half, Adebayo took a back seat to Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson, who combined to score 29 points. The Heat play three games next week, starting with the Jazz on Tuesday.

 Klay Thompson amassed 23 points (8-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and seven three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 Apparently, all Thompson needed to gain some semblance of consistency was to hit the road. He’s scored at least 19 points in three of the first four games of Miami’s five-game road trip, which concludes on Tuesday against the Jazz. On Sunday, Thompson shot 7-of-13 from beyond the arc, the third time this season he’s made at least that many triples in a game. Klay remains mainly a points and three-pointers option in fantasy leagues, but his assists and blocks were also solid against the Kings.

 Jeremiah Fears recorded 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
 Fears continues to spread his wings as the Pelicans’ point guard, scoring at least 19 points in three straight games and in five of his last six appearances.  After shooting 12-of-28 from the field in his prior three appearances, Murphy made over 50 percent of his shots on Sunday.  Williamson produced excellent percentages in his final game of the week, much to the delight of those rostering him in category leagues. Unfortunately, the production outside of the points and percentages was pretty lean in the Pelicans’ 139-123 defeat. That said, over three weeks, Williamson’s production has exceeded his ADP (69) by a safe distance. The hope is that he can avoid the extended absence that has been a common occurrence throughout his NBA career.
